wrongClaim: This round's MSI install wrote an HKLM uninstall entry while the product registered in HKCU, i.e. the package mixes per-user and per-machine contexts.
whyItWasWrong: I asserted that from an HKLM uninstall entry whose creation time I never checked, plus an /x 1605 seen in an elevated context. The installation log contradicts it.
logEvidence: PROPERTY CHANGE: Adding INSTALLDIR property. Its value is 'C:\Users\15119\AppData\Local\Programs\OpenCodeX Desktop\' - a per-user path
no ALLUSERS property change anywhere in the log
no 'Writing system registry values' record for any Uninstall key
the log covers 17:11:06 to 17:11:09 and records 'Installation completed successfully'

correctedReading.hklmUninstallEntry: not created by this install; it was an older leftover and it is now removed
correctedReading.soThePackageBehavesAsDeclared: yes for this install: InstallScope=perUser, INSTALLDIR under LocalAppData, registration in HKCU

whatRemainsUnexplained: the elevated msiexec /x against the product code returned 1605, and the uninstall only succeeded in the 15119 user context. That is consistent with the product being registered per-user while I pointed an elevated (per-machine) engine at it. It is a harness mistake, not a package defect.

HKCU\Software\gz ers\OpenCodeX Desktop\023\Components was absent after install. Not yet explained; the template declares those key-path registry values and the log shows WriteRegistryValues ran with Return value 1.
status: the earlier 'context mixing' conclusion is withdrawn. The open question is narrowed to the missing component registry values.
